extensions.sourceNote: This sidecar EXTENDS the DESIGN.md frontmatter and never duplicates it. The frontmatter (DESIGN.md lines 1-161) is the normative token layer and the single source of truth for colour values, which is why top-level `colors` is null. Everything here is what the frontmatter schema cannot hold: dark-theme counterparts, tonal ramps, shadow and motion values, breakpoints, layering, drop-in component snippets, and the document's named rules.
extensions.themeNote: Every semantic token is authored in both themes. The DESIGN.md frontmatter carries the light (:root) value; each colorMeta entry below carries its dark counterpart in `dark`. Neither theme is derived from the other. Dark is applied by an explicit [data-theme="dark"] and mirrored into prefers-color-scheme for the "system" choice.

success.note: 5.8:1 on --surface, 5.5:1 on --bg, 5.0:1 on --surface-raised. One step darker than the value it replaced, which measured 4.40:1 on --surface-raised and would have failed AA the first time a pass mark landed on a raised fill. Same hue. It is in no mirror — the terminal palette carries only the dark #57d183.

syntax-string.note: 5.59:1 on --surface-raised in light. Literally the exam terminal's own green in dark, so a YAML block in the question panel and the same YAML in the candidate's vim are the same colour.

syntax-number.note: 5.53:1 on --surface-raised in light. The exam terminal's own amber in dark. Not in the DESIGN.md frontmatter, which carries only the tokens the component layer names directly.

display.purpose: --text-hero, 3.25rem. Mono 700, 1.1, tabular. Exactly one site: the score percentage. The largest thing in the product because it is the only number the candidate came for.

headline.purpose: --text-2xl, 1.75rem. Sans 700, 1.25, -0.01em. Exactly one site: `.start-card h1`, the exam title.

title.purpose: --text-xl, 1.375rem. Sans 700, 1.25, -0.01em. The verdict (tracked to 0.12em), the score headline, the boot-panel and desktop-required headings.

data.purpose: --text-l, 1.125rem. Mono 700, 0.03em, tabular. The countdown, stat values, `.md h2`. Anything that ticks takes tabular-nums.

body.purpose: --text-m, 0.9375rem. Sans 400, 1.55. The base. 15px and not 16px: the question panel is 360px wide and shares the screen with a terminal.

secondary.purpose: --text-s, 0.85rem. The step between body and label, and the busiest non-base size in the product — about 30 sites in theme.css, including mode blurbs, bank meta, clipboard fields and hints, keyboard rows, shortcut tables, and the theme toggle. It has no frontmatter role because it is a size rather than a full type spec: it takes Sans or Mono from whatever it is labelling.

label.purpose: --text-xs, 0.75rem. Sans 600, 0.06em, uppercase. Section headings, stat labels, column heads, the bank badge, jump-grid domain heads, and the code-block language tag at 0.08em.

spacing.note: Six steps and no more — --space-1 through --space-6, carried in the frontmatter. There is no 3rem or 4rem step. Cards take --space-6 and drop to --space-4 below 600px, dialogs take --space-5, dense rows --space-1 to --space-2. Density is deliberately higher inside the exam than on the lobby and score screens: one is a working surface, the others are reading surfaces.

radii.note: Four values, carried in the frontmatter as `rounded`. --radius-xs (3px) is inline `code` only, which is also every click-to-copy value: a box sized to a few characters needs a corner proportional to itself, and nothing with real height takes it. --radius-s (6px) is anchored things, --radius-m (10px) floating things, --radius-pill status objects that are read rather than pressed. One departure: below 600px full-bleed sheets drop to radius 0, because a sheet that reaches every edge should not pretend to have corners.

shadows.name: shadow-1
shadows.purpose: The faintest lift, and one site: `.score-banner`. Dark: 0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4), 0 1px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3).

shadows.name: shadow-2
shadows.purpose: Standard card lift: `.start-card`, `.boot-panel`, `.toast`, `.desktop-required-card`, `.job-chip`. Dark: 0 4px 12px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.45), 0 2px 4px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35).

shadows.name: shadow-3
shadows.purpose: Modal depth: `.confirm-dialog`, `.control-dialog`, `.info-drawer`, `.clipboard-panel` / `.keyboard-popover`, and `.question-panel` once it becomes an overlay under 900px. Dark: 0 12px 32px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55).

motion.name: dur-quick
motion.purpose: Hover and state transitions, the scrim fade, the chevron rotation.

motion.name: dur-base
motion.purpose: The screen fade-up (4px), toasts (6px), checklist rows.

motion.name: dur-modal-in
motion.purpose: Dialogs rising 8px at a 0.99 scale, and the drawer sliding in 16px.

motion.name: dur-progress
motion.purpose: The determinate job bar, whose step has to be legible as a movement rather than a redraw. Its one use.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only curve. Decelerating, no overshoot. There is no ease-in and no exit duration: nothing in this product animates out, so those tokens were deleted rather than left declared and unused (tokens.css:174-177).

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: A literal, not a token: the translateY(1px) press on every control, deliberately below the scale's floor. The next step up (160ms) reads as a movement rather than a key-down.

motion.name: stagger-row
motion.purpose: A literal, not a token: control-checklist rows step 40ms apart and flatten at 240ms from the sixth row on, first mount only. Re-staggering on every poll would make the list feel unstable for four minutes.

breakpoints.name: panel-overlay
breakpoints.purpose: The question panel leaves the flow and becomes an overlay drawer at min(85vw, 360px) with --shadow-3, over a 36px collapsed rail. The resizer is suppressed below this width.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Dialogs and the boot panel go full-bleed (width 100%, max-height 100dvh, radius 0), the clipboard panel and keyboard popover become bottom sheets, lobby actions stack, the domain table's cells become blocks, and card padding drops one step.

breakpoints.name: coarse-pointer
breakpoints.purpose: Icon controls and the panel's --control-size go from 28px to a 44px minimum. Keyed to pointer type, not width.

layering.name: z-panel
layering.purpose: Floating controls, the question panel as a drawer, the clipboard panel, the keyboard popover, the focused skip link.

layering.name: z-dialog
layering.purpose: The confirm dialog and the About drawer.

layering.name: z-overlay
layering.purpose: The control overlay. It sits ABOVE dialogs because it blocks a destructive operation and must survive every screen transition under it.

layering.name: z-toast
layering.purpose: The toast layer and the top progress bar. Above the overlay so a confirmation is never rendered invisible.

mirrors: images/desktop/assets/terminalrc plus its xfconf twin — the exam terminal palette

icons.note: Fifteen hand-authored SVGs in ui/src/components/Icon.tsx on a 24 grid: fill none, stroke currentColor, stroke-width 1.75, round caps and joins. Sized on 1em so an icon rides the type it sits in, and always aria-hidden by construction — Icon takes no label prop, which is what stops a later call site from making an icon load-bearing.

components.name: Default Button
components.description: Every non-committing action. Hover moves the FILL one tone and the label to --accent-strong; the border never moves, because the edge is reserved for state — an accent border on hover would be the same declaration selection takes, so "the control under my pointer" and "the thing I have chosen" would draw the same outline. Disabled is --text-disabled and never opacity. Source: theme.css:7-37.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one committed action on a screen — Start Exam, Send, New Attempt. Accent fill with an --accent-contrast label (4.8:1), deepening to --accent-strong on hover. Exactly one per screen: it is one of the four things the Rare Accent Rule spends blue on. Source: theme.css:39-49.

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: End Exam, and nothing else. Danger border and label on the default fill; hover fills danger with surface-coloured text. The only control in the system that fills on hover, because ending an exam is irreversible and should feel like it commits. Source: theme.css:51-59.

components.name: Bank Card
components.description: One exam bank in the lobby catalogue, and the clearest statement of the selection model: hover is a tone step, selection is an accent edge PLUS an --accent-soft wash PLUS a 3px inset bar — the bar being the channel that survives greyscale and colour-blindness. Note the fill inversion: the card sits on --bg while the lobby card around it is --surface, which reads correctly because the page tone is darker than the card in light and lighter in dark. The third card shows the Legible Refusal: an unavailable exam is not a disabled control but a refusal with a reason, marked by `disabled`, `cursor: default`, a muted badge and an italic reason line — never by opacity, which composited that line to 3.23:1. Source: theme.css:201-289.

components.name: Question Tile
components.description: The jump grid's unit: four states on four channels, no two sharing a value. Unopened takes the structural hairline, opened the strong one (a state carried by a 1.50:1 border was the one unambiguous WCAG 1.4.11 failure in the old palette), hover moves the fill and never the edge, and the current tile adds the accent edge plus the wash plus a 3px inset bar with aria-current="true". A review mark adds a flag icon. Tiles are never labelled "answered": the UI knows it rendered the text, not that the work was done. Source: theme.css:660-730.

components.name: Mode Option (radio)
components.description: The attempt-mode picker on the lobby, and one of the four form controls in the product. A native <input type="radio"> inside a <label> row, in a borderless <fieldset> whose legend is --text-s muted. The row borrows the anchored idioms exactly — 6px, a --border hairline, a tone step on hover — and the chosen row takes an accent border plus --accent-soft, the same selection grammar as the bank card and the question tile. The blurb is not decoration: three words do not tell a candidate that Training is untimed, and one who misses that misreads their result. Source: theme.css:1443-1490, screens/Start.tsx:249-265.
components.html: How do you want to sit this?

components.name: Clipboard Textarea
components.description: The only free-text field in the product, and the fallback path for a browser that refuses navigator.clipboard. Mono at --text-s so what the candidate types here looks like what will arrive in the terminal, --surface-raised on a --border hairline, 6px, `resize: vertical`. It is always available rather than appearing after readText has already been refused — a fallback shown before it is needed is a feature; one shown after the failure is an apology. Source: theme.css:1570-1600, components/ClipboardPanel.tsx:83-97.
components.html: Type or paste here, then Send. The text lands on the exam desktop's clipboard.

components.name: Click-to-Copy Value
components.description: The system's signature component. Every inline value in a question is a button: it has to read as part of the sentence rather than as a form control, so it borrows the inline-code look exactly — --bg fill, --radius-xs, a transparent 1px border holding the space — and reveals its affordance only on hover or focus, when the border goes accent, the fill goes --accent-soft and the text goes --accent-strong. This is one of the two documented exceptions to "hover is not an accent channel", because an inline word has no resting box to tone. The copy icon is absolutely positioned out of flow: as an inline glyph at opacity 0 it still occupied its own width, so a paragraph with six copyable values read as though it had been typeset with holes in it. Source: theme.css:906-969.
components.html: Create a Namespace named on .

components.name: Instance Chip
components.description: Which box to ssh into — the single most load-bearing fact per question, and the only pill in the system carrying a full accent treatment. Mono at --text-s, --accent-strong text on --accent-soft (plain --accent is 4.0:1 on that fill), an --accent border that stays put because a border answers to WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor rather than 4.5:1. Read, never pressed: it has no hover or focus state because it is not a control. The points pill beside it is the quieter member of the same family — mono, muted ink, hairline on the page fill — and goes accent when its row is selected. Source: theme.css:612-621, 732-748.

components.name: Countdown Timer
components.description: The product's primary readout, on screen for two hours. Mono, 700, tabular-nums so a changing digit never makes a stable reading look unstable, --accent-strong on its own --surface-raised chip (plain --accent is 4.1:1 there and this is normal-size text). Under five minutes it takes --danger for both text and border and pulses — one of the three places the system permits intensity, because here intensity is information. A readout, not a control: no hover, no focus. Source: theme.css:393-420.

narrative.northStar: It is an instrument panel: it reports state accurately, never competes for attention, never performs.
narrative.overview:
The interface a person looks at while a clock they cannot pause counts down toward a result that matters to them. It is an instrument panel: it reports state accurately, never competes for attention, never performs. Three cool-slate tones, hairline borders, an accent held back until the user reaches for something, and type doing the work ornament would do elsewhere. Intensity is permitted only where intensity is information — the countdown under five minutes, a failed phase, a verdict.

One referential Kubernetes blue on slate neutrals that never drift warm. Both themes are authored; neither is derived from the other. Two faces and no third: IBM Plex Sans for prose that explains, JetBrains Mono for anything the candidate must type, match, or trust as a measurement. Depth is tone and a 1px hairline, with shadow reserved for what genuinely floats. Motion is short, decelerating, additive, and never animates out.

Nothing enforces this document — no CI check, no stylelint rule, no token test. Where it disagrees with `ui/src/styles/tokens.css` or `ui/src/theme.css`, the CSS is right.
keyCharacteristics: Kubernetes blue used referentially on cool slate, in two fully authored themes — every semantic token has a light and a dark value, and no component hardcodes a colour. No Kubernetes or CNCF mark appears anywhere.

Contrast is a ledger, not an intention: every text pairing carries its measured ratio in a comment beside the token, because jsdom has no layout engine and `axe` skips the colour-contrast rule entirely.
Monospace is a semantic choice — JetBrains Mono marks anything the candidate must type, match, or trust as a measurement, and anything that ticks takes tabular-nums.
A seven-step type scale where the top three steps have one or two sites each. A type scale is a set of permissions, not a set of quotas.
Tone and hairline borders carry depth; three shadows exist and each is reserved for something that genuinely floats above the page.
Selection is never one channel: the current object takes an accent edge plus an --accent-soft wash plus a 3px inset bar, the bar being the channel that survives greyscale and colour-blindness.

Motion is written additively inside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, so the calm state is the default rather than the fallback, and every pending state carries a channel that changes without motion.
Four form controls exist, and each earned its place. The candidate's real input surface is the terminal, so the browser UI only starts, ends, navigates and reports.

rules.name: Contrast Ledger
rules.body: every text pairing carries its measured ratio beside the token, and a pairing under 4.5:1 gets a substitute token rather than a waiver. jsdom has no layout engine, so `axe` skips contrast and the ledger is the only check (`tokens.css:13-16`)

rules.name: Rare Accent
rules.body: blue arrives for four things only — focus, currency (the selected question, the active bank, the running phase), live progress, and the one filled primary button per screen. A screen that reads as blue before it is touched has used it as decoration

rules.name: Hover is not an accent channel
rules.body: hover is one step of tone and nothing more, so the tile under a cursor never draws the outline that means "the question I am on" (`tokens.css:58-66`). Two exceptions, both elements with no resting box to tone: the click-to-copy value and the 6px panel resizer

rules.name: Two-Tier Hairline
rules.body: `--border-strong` if the edge identifies a control's hit area or carries a state, which answers WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor; `--border` for everything structural (`tokens.css:34-54`)

rules.name: Three Mirrors
rules.body: these values also live in the Go locked page (`facilitator/internal/desktop/proxy.go`), the favicon (`ui/public/favicon.svg`) and the terminal palette (`images/desktop/assets/terminalrc` plus its xfconf twin), so a colour change is never a one-file change. Grep the hex — not every token is in every mirror

rules.name: The Mono-For-Truth Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono marks anything the candidate must type, match, or trust as a measurement — names, ids, points, durations, paths, output, the score. The test is mechanical: if a value could be pasted into a terminal or compared digit by digit, it is mono.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Anything that ticks takes `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`. A digit that changes width makes a stable reading look unstable, and the countdown is on screen for two hours.

rules.name: The Three-Colour Syntax Rule
rules.body: A fenced block colours keys and keywords in `--accent-strong`, strings in `--syntax-string` and numbers in `--syntax-number`; comments take `--text-muted` and italics, and everything else inherits (`tokens.css:119-130`). The two value hues are the exam terminal's own green and amber, which makes that palette a fourth mirror.

rules.name: Unbroken Height
rules.body: `html`, `body`, `#root` and `main` all assert `height: 100%`. Do not add a wrapper to that chain without giving it a height (`base.css:8-17`)

rules.name: Scroll-Inside
rules.body: wide or long content scrolls inside its own container and never the page — tables with `overscroll-behavior-x: contain`, code blocks horizontally, and in the control dialog only the checklist while the header and actions stay pinned

rules.name: Fixed-Geometry Overlay
rules.body: overlays inside the exam screen are out of flow and never flex children, because `.desktop-pane` carries noVNC's `ResizeObserver` and any sibling geometry change costs a framebuffer round-trip

rules.name: Table-Cell
rules.body: never `display: flex` on a `<td>` or `<th>`. The cell leaves the table layout model, stops stretching to the row height and steps its `border-bottom` off its neighbours'; put the flex on a wrapper inside

rules.name: The Float-Only Rule
rules.body: Anchored to the page: tone and a hairline border. Floating above it: exactly one of the three shadows — no hover-lift, no raised button, no resting elevation in normal flow.

rules.name: The Motion-Additive Rule
rules.body: Motion is written *inside* `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, never as a default a reduce-guard later neutralises, so a reduced-motion user never depends on an animation being correctly cancelled. Layout must be identical either way: `.screen` keeps its `height: 100%` outside the media query, and every keyframe plays forward *to* the element's real style.

rules.name: The Non-Motion Channel Rule
rules.body: Every pending state carries at least one channel that changes without motion — an elapsed counter, a step label, an attempt number. Under `reduce` a stopped `.top-progress-bar` cannot be told from a decorative border, but a number that ticks reads identically in both modes.

dos: **Do** define both theme values for every new semantic token in `tokens.css`, and record the measured contrast ratio beside it. A token that exists in one theme is a bug in the other.
**Do** use `--accent-strong` for accent-coloured text on `--accent-soft` or `--surface-raised`. Plain `--accent` measures 4.0:1 and 4.1:1 there, under the floor.
**Do** reach for tone and a 1px hairline first, and add a shadow only when the element genuinely floats above the page.
**Do** set anything the candidate must type, match, or read as a measurement in JetBrains Mono, with `tabular-nums` if it changes over time.
**Do** pick radii from the four that exist: 3px inline chips only, 6px anchored, 10px floating, pill for status.
**Do** write new motion additively inside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, animating only `transform` and `opacity`.
**Do** change all three mirrors when a colour changes — the Go locked page, the favicon, and the terminal palette with its xfconf twin.
**Do** make wide content scroll inside its own container, and keep pinned whatever the user is waiting on.
**Do** open panels over the exam screen out of flow, never as a flex child. Changing `.desktop-pane`'s geometry costs a framebuffer resize mid-exam.

**Do** show a fallback path before it is needed, not after the failure. The clipboard panel is always available rather than appearing once `readText` has been refused, and the browser-reserved chords are opt-in and labelled with their caveat rather than silently enabled and silently broken.
donts: **Don't** hardcode a colour in a component. Every value comes from a semantic token, without exception.
**Don't** use the accent as a resting surface. If a screen reads as blue before the user touches anything, the accent has become decoration.
**Don't** add springs, bounces, overshoot, gradient fills, emoji, or a celebratory flourish on a pass. The product reports a result; it does not congratulate.
**Don't** build overlay tutorials, spotlight tours, or coach marks measured against live layout. Explain a screen with a self-contained drawing that holds its own proportions.
**Don't** let the score page or the lobby drift toward a dashboard — dense chrome, charts for their own sake, cards competing for attention. The score page is one column, and one number matters.
**Don't** hide an element with a `transform` when it must be keyboard-reachable. Use the `.sr-only` clip idiom.
**Don't** add a wrapper to the `html`/`body`/`#root`/`main` height chain without giving it a height.
**Don't** let `.desktop-canvas` take its size from its own content. It is absolutely positioned so noVNC's `ResizeObserver` cannot enter a resize feedback loop; that is structural, not stylistic.
**Don't** add a form control without first checking whether the interaction belongs in the terminal. Four exist, and each earned its place.

**Don't** reach for a dropdown, select or menu. The jump grid is this product's disclosure pattern and already carries more per option than a native select can render — domain grouping with the full string, points, and viewed/marked flags.
**Don't** convey a control's state with `opacity`. It dims the border and the focus ring along with the label, and composites to a ratio nobody measured. Use `--text-disabled`.
